extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent owners/applicants, and third-party requesters/practitioners handling inter partes reexamination, reissue, and interference matters
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on handling copending inter partes reexamination, reissue applications, and interference proceedings, including when to merge or stay proceedings, required notifications, permitted communications, examiner actions, and fee/participation rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination not to be delayed or stayed by interference; special dispatch
rubrics_metrics.description: The general policy of the Office is that a reexamination proceeding will not be delayed, or stayed, because of an interference. All inter partes reexamination proceedings shall be conducted with 'special dispatch' within the Office (35 U.S.C. 314(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions in an interference will take into consideration the status of the reexamination proceeding, but reexamination will ordinarily proceed; the Board has flexibility under 37 CFR 41.103 to tailor solutions where reexamination and interference are copending. Note: the reexamination proceeding itself can never be 'involved' in an interference because 35 U.S.C. 135(a) applies only to applications and patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to suspend interference under 37 CFR 41.121(a)(3)
rubrics_metrics.description: A miscellaneous motion under 37 CFR 41.121(a)(3) to suspend an interference pending the outcome of a reexamination proceeding may be made at any time during the interference by any party thereto.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The motion must be presented to the Administrative Patent Judge (APJ) who decides the motion on the facts. Suspension is not favored: normally no consideration until a reexamination order is issued and motions in the interference have been disposed of. If APJ denies the motion, a request to stay the interference may be made to the Director under 37 CFR 1.993; the Chief APJ decides such requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for reexamination filed during interference — notification duty
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 1.913, any person may, at any time during the period of enforceability of a patent, file a request for inter partes reexamination. Under 37 CFR 41.8(a), the patent owner must notify the Board that a request for reexamination was filed within twenty days of receiving notice of the request having been filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such requests will be processed normally. No delay or stay of the reexamination will occur where the third party requester is not a party to the interference or where a requester who is a party does not timely petition for a stay or delay. If the examiner orders reexamination and rejects a patent claim corresponding to a count, the attention of the Board should be called to that rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to stay reexamination because of interference — timing and propriety
rubrics_metrics.description: Any petition to stay an inter partes reexamination proceeding because of an interference filed prior to the first Office action in the reexamination proceeding will not be considered and will be returned or expunged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition to stay may be filed by the patent owner after the first Office action. If a party other than the patent owner is not the reexamination requester, any petition by that party is improper under 37 CFR 1.905 and will not be considered. Premature petitions are returned by OPLA; petitions filed subsequent to the date of the order to reexamine will be referred to OPLA on the merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to Board upon issuance/publication of reexamination certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: If one or more claims of a patent involved in an interference are canceled or amended by issuance and publication of a reexamination certificate, the Board must be promptly notified; upon issuance and publication the patent owner must notify the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issuance/publication of an inter partes reexamination certificate concludes the reexamination proceeding (37 CFR 1.997). If the certificate cancels all claims, no further Office proceedings will be conducted with that patent or related reissue applications or reexamination requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merger of concurrent reissue application and inter partes reexamination (37 CFR 1.991)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reissue application and an inter partes reexamination on which an order pursuant to §1.931 has been mailed are pending concurrently on a patent, the Office may decide to merge the two proceedings or to suspend one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When merged, the merged proceeding will be conducted in accordance with §§1.171–1.179; the patent owner must place and maintain the same claims in the reissue application and the inter partes reexamination during pendency of the merged proceeding. Examiner actions and responses by patent owner or third-party requester in a merged proceeding apply to both files; the merged inter partes reexamination shall be concluded by grant of the reissued patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party requester participation rights preserved in merged proceedings (37 CFR 1.995)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a third party requester is involved, the merger will be accomplished so as to preserve the third party requester’s right to participate to the extent provided in the regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In merged proceedings with different requesters, any paper filed by one party shall be served on all other parties. Participation is limited to issues within the scope of inter partes reexamination as provided by the regulations (see §§1.902–1.997 and 41.60–41.81).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of reissue on reexamination starting point — reissue claims as 'clean copy'
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reissue patent is to be used as the basis for reexamination, the reissue patent claims used as the starting point in the reexamination proceeding must be presented in the reexamination proceeding as a 'clean copy.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Words bracketed in the reissue patent claims would not appear in the reexamination clean copy; words added via reissue that appear in italics in the reissue patent must appear in plain format in the reexamination clean copy. Any amendment in reexamination should treat changes made by the reissue as the text of the patent (use form paragraph 22.05 where appropriate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for decision on merging or staying reissue/reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision whether to merge the examination of a reissue application and an inter partes reexamination, or to stay one of the two, will not be made prior to the mailing of the order to reexamine the patent pursuant to 37 CFR 1.931.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination on a request for reexamination should not be delayed despite a copending reissue application because 35 U.S.C. 312(a) requires a determination within three months following filing of the request. If reexamination is ordered, forward signed order (after SPRS review) to CRU support staff for mailing and notify OPLA that proceedings are ready for merger consideration; hand-deliver paper files if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations for merger vs stay — case-by-case OPLA discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision to merge or stay is made on a case-by-case basis and is within the sole discretion of the Office (OPLA) to facilitate orderly operation of proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The status of the reissue application and the reexamination proceeding (e.g., whether on appeal) will be taken into account. Where there is 'good cause' to stay the reexamination proceeding, the Director may do so pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 314(c). Issues in the reissue application that are not proper for third-party comment weigh against merger.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to maintain identical claims in merged proceedings; consequences of failure
rubrics_metrics.description: Where merger is ordered, the patent owner is required to maintain identical amendments/claims in the reissue application and the reexamination file for purposes of the merged proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If identical amendments are not present at time of merger, the patent owner will be required to submit appropriate amendments to make claims identical in both proceedings. The patent owner must not address patentability in the amendment. If required identical text is not timely submitted, any claim lacking identical text in all merged proceedings may be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, paragraph 2, as indefinite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shortened statutory periods after stay removal
rubrics_metrics.description: If a stay of a reexamination proceeding has been removed following reissue application examination, the first Office action will set a shortened statutory period for response of one month or thirty days (whichever is longer) unless a longer period is warranted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The second Office action will normally be final and will also set the shortened one month or thirty days period. These shortened periods are used to prevent undue delay and to proceed with 'special dispatch' given the earlier stay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct of merged proceeding — OPLA guidance and examiner consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision ordering merger will set forth the practice and procedure to be followed in the merged proceeding; questions should be referred to OPLA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner should consult with OPLA prior to issuing any Office action in the merged proceeding, similar to consultation required in an unmerged inter partes reexamination proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of situations where inter partes, ex parte reexamination, and reissue are copending
rubrics_metrics.description: When inter partes reexamination, ex parte reexamination, and a reissue application are copending, OPLA should be notified promptly for consideration of merger; hand-deliver paper files if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The most common sequences (reissue merged with ex parte then inter partes filed; reissue merged with inter partes then ex parte filed; inter partes merged with ex parte then reissue filed) are outlined. The decision to merge the three proceedings will provide guidance. Merger will not be carried out pursuant to MPEP Chapter 2200; prosecution prior to point of merger remains as-is.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions to merge or stay — general rule and petitions timing
rubrics_metrics.description: No petition to merge or stay is necessary because the Office will generally sua sponte make a decision to merge or stay; petitions filed prior to the determination/order to reexamine will be returned or expunged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owner may file a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 to merge or stay after the order to reexamine if Office has not acted. A third party requester does not have standing to file a petition under 1.182 to merge a reexamination proceeding with a reissue application (requester may file a notification under 1.985(b)). Any petition under 1.182 filed prior to the initial Office action must also be filed under 1.183 to waive the prohibition under 1.939(b). Petitions by improper parties will be returned or expunged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees in merged proceedings — single fee where applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Where proceedings have been merged and a paper is filed which requires payment of a fee (e.g., excess claims fee, extension of time fee, petition fees, appeal/brief/hearing fees), only a single fee need be paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: only one fee is required for an appellant brief even though multiple copies are filed for each file in the merger (as required). For excess claim fees, reissue practice will control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews prohibited in inter partes reexamination and merged proceedings (37 CFR 1.955)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 CFR 1.955, an interview which discusses the merits of a proceeding is not permitted in an inter partes reexamination proceeding. Thus, in a merged reissue/inter partes reexamination there will be no inter partes interview as to the substance, nor a separate ex parte interview as to substance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner will not conduct interviews to provide information on merits. An informal amendment by the patent owner (reissue applicant) will not be accepted as that would be tantamount to an ex parte interview. All communications directed to the merits must be in writing and filed with the Office for entry into the record; third-party requester's participation rights must be preserved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's amendment rules in merged reissue/inter partes reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: In a merged reissue/inter partes reexamination proceeding, the examiner may only make examiner’s amendments that do not require patent owner authorization (formal matters) in conjunction with a Notice of Allowability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted examiner’s amendments include formal matters such as grammar, spelling, incorrect numbering, or title changes. Any change going to the merits cannot be made by examiner’s amendment; it requires (A) reopening of prosecution with CRU Director approval, (B) an Office action suggesting the change to the patent owner/reissue applicant, (C) a formal amendment by the patent owner/reissue applicant, and (D) an opportunity for the third party requester to comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination certificate/reissued patent effects (37 CFR 1.997 / 1.991)
rubrics_metrics.description: To conclude an inter partes reexamination proceeding, the Director will issue and publish an inter partes reexamination certificate setting forth results. If the reexamination is terminated by the grant of a reissued patent as provided in §1.991, the reissued patent will constitute the reexamination certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a certificate cancels all claims of the patent, no further Office proceedings will be conducted with that patent or any reissue applications or reexamination requests relating thereto.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue application examination treatment and Office policy re concurrency
rubrics_metrics.description: A reissue application will be examined in the same manner as a non-reissue, non-provisional application; reissue applications will be acted on by the examiner in advance of other applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General policy: examination of a reissue application and an inter partes reexamination will not be conducted separately for a particular patent to permit timely resolution and to prevent inconsistent/conflicting amendments. The decision to merge or stay is made in OPLA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of concurrent proceedings filing duties (37 CFR 1.178(b), 1.565(a), 1.985)
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner should file a Notification of Concurrent Proceedings in the reissue application (37 CFR 1.178(b)) and in the reexamination proceeding (37 CFR 1.565(a) or 1.985) as early as possible to notify the Office of the existence of the concurrent proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If paper files exist, they should be hand delivered to OPLA when notifying OPLA that the proceedings are ready for consideration of merger.

rubrics_metrics.name: When reissue is pending at reexamination request decision time
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reissue patent will not be granted prior to expiration of the three-month period for making the determination on the reexamination request, a decision will be made after an order to reexamine as to whether the reissue application examination and the reexamination proceeding are to be merged, or which of the two (if any) is to be stayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this situation, no first Office action will have accompanied the order for reexamination. Consider whether issues in the reissue application are proper for third-party comment; if not, merger ordinarily will not be ordered and one proceeding will be stayed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision factors when reissue application filed after reexamination ordered
rubrics_metrics.description: When a reissue application is filed after an inter partes reexamination request has been filed (or reexamination already ordered), OPLA should be notified promptly and a determination made whether reexamination should be ordered or whether to consider merger.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reexamination was already ordered prior to filing the reissue application, OPLA should be notified that proceedings are ready for consideration of merger; paper files should be hand delivered. Consider whether issues are proper for third-party comment and the status of the reexamination (e.g., on appeal or notice of intent to issue certificate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel/prohibition on subsequent inter partes reexamination after certain final civil or reexamination decisions (35 U.S.C. 317)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a final decision has been entered in a civil action that a party has not sustained its burden of proving invalidity of any patent claim, or if a final decision in an inter partes reexamination instituted by a third-party requester is favorable to the patentability of any original or proposed amended/new claim, then that party and its privies may not thereafter request an inter partes reexamination of any such patent claim on the basis of issues which the party or its privies raised or could have raised in such civil action or inter partes reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This subsection does not prevent assertion of invalidity based on newly discovered prior art unavailable to the third-party requester and the PTO at the time of the inter partes reexamination proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of inter partes reexamination due to litigation (37 CFR 1.987)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent in the process of inter partes reexamination is or becomes involved in litigation, the Director shall determine whether or not to suspend the inter partes reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts may stay litigation upon issuance of an order for inter partes reexamination unless the court determines a stay would not serve the interests of justice (35 U.S.C. 318).
